dataset.name: Wikipedia-discovered Wikidata candidates
dataset.description: Bounded English Wikipedia search windows and corresponding Wikidata items. Proposals only; no canonical identity, employment or financial attribution.

endpoints.name: wikipedia_search
endpoints.response_root: query.pages; generator=search, namespace 0, five hits, pageprops and revision identifiers/timestamps

endpoints.name: wikidata_entities
endpoints.response_root: entities; wbgetentities over exactly the observed page QIDs, English labels/descriptions/aliases, all claims and enwiki sitelinks

acquisition.pagination: One five-hit search window per exact reported string. Preserve continuation raw; do not follow it or claim exhaustive search. Missing links and missing entities remain explicit.

partitions.name: capture
partitions.source: Exact query JSON digest and build identity
partitions.purpose: Retain independent observation evidence without changing FEC releases or graph generations.

acquisition.retry_policy: No automatic retries. At most twenty queries and forty serial requests, at least one second apart, 30 seconds/request and five minutes/run. Four MiB/body, 64 MiB/run, 128 KiB/response headers. Fixed HTTPS origins, no redirects, no proxy inheritance, no credentials. Send descriptive user-agent and maxlag=5. Save bounded failed bodies and attempt metadata; stop network calls after the first HTTP, transport or schema failure. Restart explicitly into a new directory.

physical_schema.encoding: Strict UTF-8 JSON; reject duplicate keys, unpaired surrogates, excessive depth and trailing JSON.
physical_schema.null_policy: Do not treat API failures as no matches. Missing items use the source missing flag. Incomplete page metadata blocks use. Raw null/empty forms remain in captured bytes.
physical_schema.schema_fingerprint: Compiled closed envelopes and selected term/identity shapes in internal/source/wikimedia. Claims, sitelinks, limits and continuation retain opaque JSON under the explicit structural contract. Record each observed JSON path/type fingerprint in offline replay; never adopt remote schema changes automatically.

identity.publisher_record_key: Wikipedia pageid plus revision metadata; Wikidata QID plus lastrevid. Neither is a FEC identity.
identity.occurrence_locator: Capture digest, query ordinal, exact request URL and response body digest; page ID or QID within that response.
identity.record_version: Exact response SHA-256 and publisher revision metadata. Cross-endpoint observations are not an atomic snapshot.
identity.duplicate_policy: Retain every query's observation. Reject repeated page IDs/ranks and duplicate JSON keys. Deduplicate only identical query text while retaining each original FEC source reference.

time_fields.meaning: Client request time, not validity of an employment or ownership relationship.
Preserve publisher revision and qualified statement time separately from FEC source cycles.

rules: Wikipedia search discovers candidates; its order is not identity confidence. Separately versioned name rules propose QIDs only within the saved search window; source acquisition does not approve identity.

The v1 proposal baseline normalizes case and punctuation only. The separate v2 proposal policy adds explained letter/number boundaries and bounded trailing legal-designator variants. Both retain original source text, token order and accents; neither uses fuzzy, embedding or LLM rules. See docs/design/organization-resolution.md for the derived policy contract; source response schemas are unchanged.
Exclude Wikipedia disambiguation pages and explicit nondeprecated direct P31=Q5 human claims from organization proposals. Other types remain unverified; no subclass closure is inferred.
Preserve all returned claims, ranks, qualifiers and references. Do not convert P112/P169 or any other property into outgoing donor-to-company edges.
No person merge, employment verification, ownership verification, graph publication or terminal dollar allocation is authorized by this output.

revisions.publisher_model: Mutable community-curated data and search indexes. Search and entity requests occur at different times.
revisions.effective_projection: No current identity projection. Saved responses replay under a separate versioned proposal policy; refresh and reviewed corroboration remain future work.

checks.rule: Pin manifest and query digests; verify confined regular body files, size/hash, exact reconstructed requests and request/byte budgets.
Retain invalid bodies, but do not use API errors, warnings, schema drift, incomplete entities or failed/truncated requests as negative search evidence.
Name matches remain proposals. Missing QIDs, missing entities and competing name matches cannot become singleton identity decisions.

use.retention: Retain raw capture and exact source/build identities for offline replay. API failures are evidence of a failed observation, not entity absence.
use.disclaimer: Community-curated candidate evidence, not authoritative corporate identity or verified financial connection. Respect upstream licensing and attribution when displaying source content.
